proof:
# Sharp convex-order contraction for vertex averaging on a simplex

Let Delta_d={x in R^d:x_i>=0,sum x_i=1}, with normalized uniform
(d-1)-dimensional volume mu_d, where d>=2. Let Z have law mu_d and
let I be independent and uniform in {1,...,d}. Set

    Y_b=(1-b)Z+b e_I, 0<=b<=1.

Then the exact range for the convex-order contraction is

    Y_b <=_cx Z  if and only if  0<=b<=1/d.            (1)

In particular every continuous concave psi on Delta_d satisfies

    (1/d) sum_i int psi((1-b)z+b e_i) dmu_d(z)
                         >= int psi(z) dmu_d(z)      (2)

throughout this range. The proof constructs a martingale coupling at
the critical b=1/d, meaning a joint law (Y,X) with Y distributed as
Y_(1/d), X distributed as Z, and E[X|Y]=Y. It uses only elementary
simplex-volume densities and conditional expectation. No ordinary
depth theorem or assumed convex-order statement is used.

## 1. An elementary random-step merging lemma

For any integer m>=1, let W be uniform on Delta_m, J uniform among
its m vertices, and R independent with density

    m(1-r)^(m-1), 0<r<1.

Put

    X=(1-R)W+R e_J,
    V=(m/(m+1))W+e_J/(m+1).                          (3)

Then X is uniform on Delta_m and E[X|V]=V.

For m>=2, condition on J=j,R=r. The image simplex has density
(1-r)^(-(m-1)) on {x_j>=r} relative to mu_m. Integrating the
displayed density of R gives the conditional density m*x_j for
X given J=j. Averaging over j gives sum_j x_j=1, proving uniformity.
Also E[R]=1/(m+1), so E[X|W,J]=V. Since V is a function of (W,J),
the tower property gives E[X|V]=V. For m=1 the simplex is a point
and every assertion is immediate, with the same formulas.

This is also the familiar construction that splits a Dirichlet
weight and then merges it into a uniformly chosen coordinate, but
no Dirichlet classification is required for the proof.

## 2. The critical law in minimum-coordinate cells

Put b_*=1/d and rho=(d-1)/d. Conditional on I=i, the affine map
Z ->rho Z+e_i/d has volume Jacobian rho^(d-1). Therefore Y=Y_b*
has density relative to mu_d

    f(y)=N(y)/(d rho^(d-1)),
    N(y)=#{i:y_i>=1/d}.                              (4)

Boundaries have mu_d-measure zero; their counting convention does not
affect this law. The law has no singular boundary component.

Partition Delta_d, outside the null set of tied minimum coordinates,
into the cells P_i={y:y_i<y_j for every j!=i}. Their closures are
the simplices

    conv(g,{e_j:j!=i}), g=(1/d,...,1/d).

Their uniform masses are1/d. By permutation symmetry the law (4)
also gives each P_i mass1/d. Consequently its conditional density
on P_i, relative to the conditional uniform law on that cell, is
still f(y), with no extra normalization factor.

On a fixed cell introduce coordinates

    t=d y_i,
    w_j=(y_j-y_i)/(1-t), j!=i,
    y_i=t/d, y_j=t/d+(1-t)w_j.                       (5)

The point t=1 is the single centroid and can be ignored. Under the
uniform law on the cell, t has density

    (d-1)(1-t)^(d-2), 0<t<1,

and w is independently uniform on Delta_(d-1). This follows directly
by the affine barycentrics of the cell: t and the coordinates
(1-t)w_j sum to one; their slice Jacobian is (1-t)^(d-2).

For y in the cell, y_i<1/d. For j!=i, (5) gives the exact equivalence

    y_j>=1/d  if and only if  w_j>=1/d.

Thus (4) depends only on w. Moreover

    d rho^(d-1)=(d-1)rho^(d-2).                      (6)

It follows that, conditional on the minimum-coordinate label i,
t keeps the preceding Beta(1,d-1) law and is independent of w,
while the w law has density

    #{j:w_j>=1/d}/[(d-1)rho^(d-2)]                   (7)

relative to uniform on Delta_(d-1). This is EXACTLY the vertex
averaging law (3) called V, in m=d-1 coordinates, with step
1/(m+1)=1/d. For d=2, m=1 and this is the point law.

## 3. Explicit reconstruction of the martingale

Here is a complete sampling construction. Independently choose:

* a label L uniform in {1,...,d};
* T with density (d-1)(1-t)^(d-2) on (0,1);
* W uniform on Delta_(d-1), whose coordinates are indexed by j!=L;
* J uniformly among those d-1 coordinates;
* R with density (d-1)(1-r)^(d-2) on (0,1).

Use the lower-dimensional merging lemma to define

    V=rho W+e_J/d,
    X_face=(1-R)W+R e_J.

Reconstruct vectors Y,X in Delta_d by

    Y_L=X_L=T/d,
    Y_j=T/d+(1-T)V_j,       j!=L,
    X_j=T/d+(1-T)X_face,j,  j!=L.                    (8)

Section2 proves that Y has exactly the law of Y_(1/d). The merging
lemma makes X_face uniform, independent of T. Hence X conditional
on L is uniform on the minimum cell P_L, and mixing L makes X
uniform on all Delta_d.

Furthermore E[X_face|W,J]=V. Conditioning on (L,T,W,J) in (8)
gives E[X|L,T,W,J]=Y. Since Y is a function of those variables,
the tower property proves E[X|Y]=Y. This establishes the critical
convex-order assertion constructively. No common fixed minimum-cell
label for the ORIGINAL independent pair (Z,I) is assumed; (8) is a
new coupling with the exact two required marginals.

## 4. Smaller parameters, sharpness, and equality examples

For 0<=b<=1/d, put theta=db. With the ORIGINAL independent pair
(Z,I), one has pointwise

    Y_b=(1-theta)Z+theta Y_(1/d).

For convex phi, Jensen and the critical result give

    E phi(Y_b)<=(1-theta)E phi(Z)+theta E phi(Y_(1/d))
                                             <=E phi(Z).

Negating phi gives (2). The case b=0 is the identity. For d=2 at
b=1/2, the two affine half-interval images partition the interval,
so Y_(1/2) has EXACTLY the uniform law. This also follows from
the m=1 reconstruction in Section3.

For sharpness use the continuous concave function

    psi(x)=min_i x_i.

For any k chosen coordinates of uniform Z, translation of those
coordinates gives

    P(min_(chosen k) Z_i>=s)=(1-ks)_+^(d-1),
    E min_(chosen k) Z_i=1/(dk).                    (9)

If b>=1/d, the raised coordinate of Y_b is at least b, while the
smallest among its other coordinates is at most (1-b)/(d-1)<=b.
It is therefore always one of the unraised coordinates. Equation(9)
gives exactly

    E psi(Y_b)=(1-b)/[d(d-1)],
    E psi(Z)=1/d^2.                                (10)

The former is strictly smaller for every b>1/d. Hence (2), and
therefore convex-order contraction, fail there. This proves the
if-and-only-if in (1), not merely a sufficient interval.

At b=1/d the entire MINIMUM-coordinate distribution is preserved:
from (9), both survival functions equal (1-ds)_+^(d-1). The explicit
coupling (8) preserves the minimum and its label pointwise. Thus
nonaffine concave functions such as min_i x_i have equality at the
critical parameter. No strictness or quantitative affine extraction
is inferred at that parameter.

## 5. A limited observation about independent random steps

For m>=3, suppose an independent step B has an absolutely continuous
probability density w on[0,1], and uniform W and independent uniform J
make (1-B)W+B e_J uniform again. Then necessarily

    w(b)=m(1-b)^(m-1) almost everywhere.

Indeed G(x)=int_0^x w(b)/(1-b)^(m-1) db is continuous for x<1,
G(0)=0, and the output density condition gives sum_j G(x_j)=m.
Continuity extends that identity from almost every interior point to
every interior point and then to boundary points by limits. Comparing
(x,y,1-x-y,0,...) and (x+y,1-x-y,0,...) gives
G(x)+G(y)=G(x+y). Monotonicity yields G(x)=m*x, and differentiation
proves the density formula. This observation concerns densities only.
If an atom at0 is permitted, every mixture of delta0 and that Beta
law is also stationary. For m=2, deterministic B=1/2 is another
stationary law. No unrestricted uniqueness claim is made.

This optional observation is not used in the critical coupling.
Section3, rather than a change in the independent random-step mean,
supplies the sharper result.
